answer: The cheapest real defence: let the challenge probing adapt: it keeps issuing tasks the fleet already failed, because horizon only stays cheap while repeat infrastructure gets no useful signal and its pass rate degrades each epoch. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
